svg.text: Rail bus layout — 3 two-row bands, 5 straight wires, zero crossings
Rail bus layout — 3 two-row bands, 5 straight wires, zero crossings
Every hole is isolated (plated-through = pads on both faces, not neighbours joined). Each bus is ONE fully stripped BARE solid wire lying flat
Every hole is isolated (plated-through = pads on both faces, not neighbours joined). Each bus is ONE fully stripped BARE solid wire lying flat
along ONE row, soldered into every hole in its span. Bare is safe because nothing crosses: in that span every hole is this bus's or nobody's.
along ONE row, soldered into every hole in its span. Bare is safe because nothing crosses: in that span every hole is this bus's or nobody's.
Row A: 13.8 V (cols 1–21) · SDA (cols 26–31). Row B: GND (cols 1–23) · SCL (cols 26–31). Row C: 3V3 (cols 21–31).
Row A: 13.8 V (cols 1–21) · SDA (cols 26–31). Row B: GND (cols 1–23) · SCL (cols 26–31). Row C: 3V3 (cols 21–31).
All five buses: fully stripped ~22 AWG SOLID core (breadboard jumper stock). One gauge does the lot — 22 AWG carries ~7 A against a ~2.4 A peak.
All five buses: fully stripped ~22 AWG SOLID core (breadboard jumper stock). One gauge does the lot — 22 AWG carries ~7 A against a ~2.4 A peak.
⚠ Row B carries TWO nets — GND ends col 23, SCL starts col 26. With BARE wire, cols 24–25 (~5 mm) are the ONLY isolation: GND ↔ SCL must read OPEN.

ALL 13 connectors kept, PCA and TMP102 taps stay SEPARATE as in the permanent design. 13 slots: six pairs at 2-column spacing, plus one single at col 31.

LEGEND — every connector on this variant is JST-XH; bodies are drawn to scale

Baseline rail uses 0.1" pin headers at cols 1-3 / 5-7. This variant replaces them with JST-XH — the stock on the bench.
Baseline rail uses 0.1" pin headers at cols 1-3 / 5-7. This variant replaces them with JST-XH — the stock on the bench.
JST-XH header. RED TAB = the LATCH/wide side. Within a pair the tabs point OUTWARD — the headers are MIRRORED.
JST-XH header. RED TAB = the LATCH/wide side. Within a pair the tabs point OUTWARD — the headers are MIRRORED.
BODY FACE: every connector is body-IN (body on the INNER, cylinder-centre face) EXCEPT the two drawn with a RED body — those are BODY-OUT, through the sidewall.

TEMPORARY STOPGAP — NOT the design of record. The permanent rail is rail_bus_overlay.svg (0.1" pin headers at cols 1-3 / 5-7). Build THIS in India, revert in the USA.
TEMPORARY STOPGAP — NOT the design of record. The permanent rail is rail_bus_overlay.svg (0.1" pin headers at cols 1-3 / 5-7). Build THIS in India, revert in the USA.
Why it exists: the permanent design needs 2-pin 0.1" pin headers for the six driver landings, none are in hand, and Chail delivery is 10 days against an 8-day stay. 2-pin JST-XH is on the bench.

PAIRED HEADERS — the bench finding that keeps every connector (2026-09-09).
PAIRED HEADERS — the bench finding that keeps every connector (2026-09-09).
Connectors go in SIX MIRRORED PAIRS at 2-column spacing, the next pair starting 5 columns on, plus one single at col 31: 1,3 | 6,8 | 11,13 | 16,18 | 21,23 | 26,28 | 31.
Connectors go in SIX MIRRORED PAIRS at 2-column spacing, the next pair starting 5 columns on, plus one single at col 31: 1,3 | 6,8 | 11,13 | 16,18 | 21,23 | 26,28 | 31.
Rail #1 uses 12 slots and rail #2 all 13, so NOTHING IS DROPPED. PWR OUT / SIG OUT stay fitted so rail #1 still serves both SKUs, and the PCA and TMP102 taps stay separate.
Rail #1 uses 12 slots and rail #2 all 13, so NOTHING IS DROPPED. PWR OUT / SIG OUT stay fitted so rail #1 still serves both SKUs, and the PCA and TMP102 taps stay separate.
WHY IT WORKS: the XH pin is OFF-CENTRE in the body — about 2.5 mm to one edge and 3.2 mm to the other (scaled off eXH.pdf p.2). So the body is not symmetric about its pin row.
WHY IT WORKS: the XH pin is OFF-CENTRE in the body — about 2.5 mm to one edge and 3.2 mm to the other (scaled off eXH.pdf p.2). So the body is not symmetric about its pin row.
Mirror a pair NARROW-SIDE-TO-NARROW-SIDE and it needs 2.5 + 2.5 = 5.0 mm against the 5.08 mm two columns give — it fits by 0.08 mm. Between pairs the WIDE sides face each other and
Mirror a pair NARROW-SIDE-TO-NARROW-SIDE and it needs 2.5 + 2.5 = 5.0 mm against the 5.08 mm two columns give — it fits by 0.08 mm. Between pairs the WIDE sides face each other and
need 3.2 + 3.2 = 6.4 mm against 7.62, clearing by 1.22. That 0.08 mm is why this is a bench discovery and not a CAD one.
need 3.2 + 3.2 = 6.4 mm against 7.62, clearing by 1.22. That 0.08 mm is why this is a bench discovery and not a CAD one.
** ORIENTATION IS LOAD-BEARING. Fit one header of a pair the wrong way round and narrow meets wide: 5.7 mm needed against 5.08 — it INTERFERES by 0.62 mm and will not seat. **
** ORIENTATION IS LOAD-BEARING. Fit one header of a pair the wrong way round and narrow meets wide: 5.7 mm needed against 5.08 — it INTERFERES by 0.62 mm and will not seat. **
The RED TAB on each connector marks the LATCH / wide side. Within every pair the two tabs point OUTWARD, away from each other. That is not only the clearance rule — the latch lives on the wide
The RED TAB on each connector marks the LATCH / wide side. Within every pair the two tabs point OUTWARD, away from each other. That is not only the clearance rule — the latch lives on the wide
side, so mirroring narrow-in also throws both latches outward where a finger can reach them. Latches facing INTO a 0.08 mm gap would be unreleasable.
side, so mirroring narrow-in also throws both latches outward where a finger can reach them. Latches facing INTO a 0.08 mm gap would be unreleasable.
Caliper check before soldering: measure body depth and pin offset on one header. The pair needs 2 x (narrow side) <= 5.08 mm and the gap needs 2 x (wide side) <= 7.62 mm.
Caliper check before soldering: measure body depth and pin offset on one header. The pair needs 2 x (narrow side) <= 5.08 mm and the gap needs 2 x (wide side) <= 7.62 mm.
Three bands, five bare bus wires, zero crossings, one straight run per row, 31 columns, and the build order: connectors and headers FIRST, buses LAST.
Three bands, five bare bus wires, zero crossings, one straight run per row, 31 columns, and the build order: connectors and headers FIRST, buses LAST.
13.8 V row A cols 1-21 . GND row B cols 1-23 . 3V3 row C cols 21-31 . SDA row A cols 26-31 . SCL row B cols 26-31.
13.8 V row A cols 1-21 . GND row B cols 1-23 . 3V3 row C cols 21-31 . SDA row A cols 26-31 . SCL row B cols 26-31.
Row A firebreak cols 22-25 (4 columns). Row B firebreak cols 24-25 - TWO columns, 5.08 mm, as tight as the permanent design. GND <-> SCL OPEN is still the acceptance check.
Row A firebreak cols 22-25 (4 columns). Row B firebreak cols 24-25 - TWO columns, 5.08 mm, as tight as the permanent design. GND <-> SCL OPEN is still the acceptance check.
Every connector pin was checked to land on exactly one wire: no pin on a bare hole, no wire reaching a foreign net.
Every connector pin was checked to land on exactly one wire: no pin on a bare hole, no wire reaching a foreign net.
The 3-pin window is cols 26-31 and holds exactly the three that rail #1 needs: SIG OUT 26, SIG IN 28, PACK SIG 31. Rail #2 puts its two I2C taps at 26 and 28 and SIG IN at 31.

One thing the stopgap does BETTER than the permanent design.

The permanent rail pushes an XH housing onto a bare 0.1" pin - friction only, nothing to latch to, on twelve 13.8 V connections in a handheld unit. Here every mate is XH into XH shroud, latched.
